title: Calibration of Time-Series Forecasting: Detecting and Adapting Context-Driven Distribution Shift

problem.claim: Time-series forecasting models are susceptible to distribution shifts driven by observed or unobserved temporal contexts, causing context-specific prediction bias.

gap.claim: Context-driven distribution shift poses challenges for conventional training paradigms, motivating calibration methods for trained models.

contributions.claim: A universal calibration methodology is introduced for detecting and adapting context-driven distribution shift in trained forecasting models.
Reconditionor detects vulnerability to context-driven distribution shift by measuring mutual information between prediction residuals and corresponding contexts.
SOLID adapts a model by curating a contextually similar dataset for a test sample and fine-tuning the prediction layer with limited steps.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Reconditionor as a novel context-driven distribution-shift detector.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the adaptation strategy can achieve an optimal bias-variance trade-off.
The authors report that Reconditionor and SOLID are model-agnostic and adaptable to a wide range of models.
Extensive experiments reportedly show that SOLID consistently improves current forecasting models on real-world datasets, especially when substantial shift is detected by Reconditionor.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deep learning models have become successful in time-series forecasting.
Forecasting models are vulnerable to temporal-context-driven distribution shifts, which create context-specific prediction bias and challenge conventional training.
The proposed Reconditionor detects susceptibility by evaluating mutual information between residuals and contexts; higher scores indicate more severe susceptibility.
SOLID calibrates the model using contextually similar samples and limited fine-tuning of the prediction layer.
The abstract reports theoretical and experimental support for the adaptation strategy and its broad model applicability.

unknowns: Evaluated datasets, forecasting models, baselines, metrics, and numerical results are unspecified.
Theoretical assumptions and the meaning of optimal bias-variance trade-off are unspecified.
Reconditionor thresholds, SOLID hyperparameters, sample sizes, and computational costs are unspecified.
The extent of performance gains and failure cases are unspecified.
